reasoning: The December 2015 meeting marks the exit from the zero lower bound (ZLB) that had been in place since December 2008, with the directive explicitly raising the federal funds rate target from '0 to 1/4 percent' to '1/4 to 1/2 percent' — a textbook ZLB exit event. The prior document still held the rate at 0-25 bps and was assessing 'whether it will be appropriate to raise the target range at its next meeting,' while the current document executes that first hike and inaugurates a new tightening regime with 'gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy.'
